title: Quiet Table
summary: A calm table: the stone board, two text strips, one voice line, the moves (folded on a phone) and a hairline row of Hint, Undo and Menu. Help shows only under a finger, and the game has one strong moment: the king lies down.
problem: Today the game screen shows many controls, panels and a long move list at once. The painted figures and the special moves must compete with chrome for the eye.
idea: Take everything off the table that a turn does not need. The board is the stage; one line of plain words speaks for the game; a hold reads a piece and shows its reach; Moves, settings and Extra fold away.

borrows.what: Only the board and the clocks. King Down keeps the same calm, but its new pieces still explain themselves on a hold.
A quiet frame with one focal point. Here the focal point is the painted board.
The cause line: a thin line from the piece that acts to the square it hits, so a shot over pieces is never a surprise.

borrows.from: Hearthstone and Marvel Snap card zoom
borrows.what: Hold to read. The piece's line goes in the voice line, not in a card frame over the board.

options.name: Light floor
options.summary: The board on a warm parchment table, lit from above. The advisors' Still Table and Open Table.

options.name: Dark stage
options.summary: The board on the warm dark stage of the title screen. The board glows like a lamp-lit table.

recommendation: Use A, the light floor, as the default: it reads best in daylight, and both advisors pick it. Let the floor follow the device's dark mode, so B costs almost nothing. Owner check: offer Light and Dark in the Menu?
notes: Look at the rest state first: nothing on the table but the game. Then press Replay: hold, shot, check with its cause line, and the king lies down.
Hold any piece (long press, mouse rest, or the I key) to see where it can take; the voice line gives its rule. A hold never plays a move. The read-own state holds your Archer on a3.
Coordinates show only while you hold or drag a piece, or while the keyboard is on the board. Freeze is the one power control, in your strip.
On a phone the Moves line is folded. On a desktop the list stays open in soft ink, with the newest move at the bottom. The board never moves.
On a phone the board gets smaller only when the screen is short (a phone browser with its toolbars), so the words under it always have room.

At the end the king lies down in its own square, on a soft pool of warm light. On a phone, Review folds the result to one line and gives the moves the space. On a desktop the list is already open, so the end shows only Rematch.

The demo plays the real rules and the Casual computer from P1. New game in Menu deals a random army with the same two kings. Rematch starts the same army (RABOGMKS, a back rank that fits P1) from move 1.
The Light and Dark choice in Menu is an addition to the direction. It waits for the owner's check.
P2 cannot come after the scripted line (pawns are back on f2 and a5), so the video says "Another game, near the end."
Limits: Guide and the Extra pages are not built here. The sounds are the kit's tones, not the stone sounds of the direction.
With the focus on the page, the left and right arrow keys step through the states.
